dimension_policy.novelty: Only O-overlap observations are recorded here; formal novelty scoring remains separate.
dimension_policy.evidence_strength: No evidence-strength tier is assigned here; evidence references point only to originating clean-worker artifacts.
dimension_policy.decision_relevance: Judged independently from novelty/evidence using fit to current O uncertainty, expected information value, implementation/evaluation tractability, overlap, and decision impact.

input_integrity_note.handling: Excluded completely from relevance judgments. AgentRewind relevance below uses only the clean long_horizon worker artifact and O read-only state.

active_decision_context: O minimizes defensible expected elapsed time to real-world AGI and treats O as instrumental/replaceable.

O already has scoped reversible Candidates, regression/rollback contracts, deterministic journals, source-bound Context Kernel manifests, protected held-out machinery, and exact negative-evidence scope policy.
O still has zero independent external evaluation evidence as a major bottleneck.

The current native Execute is a revision-22-bound matched behavioral action-adherence comparison between the current Context Kernel route and a manifest-free control; verbal/static understanding is explicitly insufficient.
Clean_g1 feed ingestion occurs only at safe semantic boundaries and must not create extra Work invocations solely for feed polling.

highest_current_value_clusters: behavioral action-adherence and active mutable-state evaluation rather than static retrieval/proxy metrics
benchmark/scaffold/verifier integrity under optimization, contamination, and realistic environment faults
adaptive evaluation-budget allocation and decision-discriminating experiment choice
scoped rollback with aligned context/environment or dependency-local invalidation
compute-matched self-improvement acceptance, activation/adherence measurement, and cross-domain negative-transfer control
conditional search/topology/diversity allocation rather than raw agent count or one universal search strategy

self_improvement.o_fit: O already requires held-out/regression evidence, but compute-matched direct-search baselines for persistent harness evolution are not yet a demonstrated routine control.
self_improvement.scope: Harness-evolution studies with unit-test and disjoint held-out comparisons; not a claim that persistent improvement never transfers.
self_improvement.uncertainty: Benchmark and scaffold dependence remains high; exact benefit of each acceptance protocol in O is untested.
self_improvement.decision_use: For self-improvement claims, compare against compute-matched direct sampling/refinement and disjoint held-out evaluation before crediting persistent harness changes.

self_improvement.o_fit: O already uses bounded Candidates and empirical regression gates; the clean evidence directly supports keeping empirical regression checks because self-attributed regressions are poorly predicted.
self_improvement.scope: Agentic harness engineering on the reported TerminalBench/SWE transfer settings; same-benchmark gains do not imply broad transfer.
self_improvement.uncertainty: Component interactions are non-additive and the strongest same-benchmark gain transfers only weakly to SWE in the reported frozen test.
self_improvement.decision_use: Preserve empirical regression gates and require frozen transfer tests; do not replace them with model-predicted fixes/regressions.

self_improvement.o_fit: O's current active unit is explicitly measuring action adherence; the worker evidence says artifact creation/update can be much less limiting than activation, following, and conditional success.
self_improvement.scope: Tested harness-update settings and models; not proof that activation is always the dominant bottleneck.
self_improvement.uncertainty: Activation and solver capability interact, so a universal activation threshold is unsupported.
self_improvement.decision_use: Instrument self-improvement as update/extraction -> activation/adherence -> task outcome, and avoid spending more improver compute before locating the failing stage.

self_improvement.o_fit: O already changes methods when evidence stalls; meta-evolution evidence adds a concrete warning that extra meta-search can yield near-zero gain in low-signal regimes.
self_improvement.scope: HSI's reported BabyAI/Crafter/TextWorld/MiniHack/NLE settings; not unrestricted recursive self-improvement.
self_improvement.uncertainty: Feedback fidelity and reachable capability are confounded with environment family.
self_improvement.decision_use: Condition meta-improvement budget on feedback signal and headroom rather than running meta-search uniformly.

self_improvement.o_fit: O has scoped Candidates but lacks demonstrated supervision-type routing for persistent artifacts; reported off-domain negative transfer makes this directly relevant to admission policy.
self_improvement.scope: GDPevo task groups and supervision modes; gold-answer/few-shot specialization versus on-policy feedback transfer is not universal.
self_improvement.uncertainty: Creator complexity is not causally isolated from solver/model effects in all cells.
self_improvement.decision_use: Evaluate persistent artifacts across target domains and prefer context-specific admission/fallback; separate supervision type from artifact-generator sophistication.

self_improvement.o_fit: O already preserves best Candidates and regression evidence; BaT adds evidence that targeted repair alone can miss anti-forgetting and end-to-end coordination needs.
self_improvement.scope: BiCuRL/medical benchmark training setup; does not isolate each curriculum component or imply GRPO belongs in O.
self_improvement.uncertainty: Stage routing, checkpoint fallback, algorithm choice, and three training pools are not individually causally separated.
self_improvement.decision_use: If O adopts training-like self-improvement, evaluate targeted repair together with protected rehearsal/global-coordination controls rather than only target weakness score.

long_horizon.o_fit: O's Context Kernel controls source updates and routing, but current evidence is stronger on provenance than on active mutable-state competence; GAMBIT directly tests update, interference, binding, and revision failures that static retrieval misses.
long_horizon.scope: Deterministic game-style active-memory tasks and tested model set; passive retrieval divergence is not a universal ranking result.
long_horizon.uncertainty: Transfer from games to repository-scale work requires matched O tasks.
long_horizon.decision_use: Add or select behavioral tests that require state mutation/revision and interference control, not only retrieval or verbal recall.

long_horizon.o_fit: O already has restart-safe journals and side-effect boundaries; aligned restoration of agent context plus reversible workspace state with retained failure lesson is a direct recovery-mechanism candidate.
long_horizon.scope: Long-horizon engineering tasks with controlled workspace rollback; network/external-service/process side effects outside the workspace are explicitly irreversible.
long_horizon.uncertainty: Worker-state exact table values were not all primary-verified at its checkpoint; checkpoint cost and independent replication remain open.
long_horizon.decision_use: Test whether O recovery restores coherent decision context and reversible environment together while retaining a compact failed-branch lesson; keep external effects outside rollback claims.

long_horizon.o_fit: O already has source clocks, dependency bindings, invalidation, and immutable replay, making dependency-local invalidation/replay highly tractable without requiring global restart.
long_horizon.scope: Typed memory-to-action provenance and controlled recovery benchmarks; does not prove uniformly better trace reconstruction.
long_horizon.uncertainty: Applicability depends on trustworthy dependency edges and distinguishing reversible recomputation from external effects.
long_horizon.decision_use: Compare selective descendant invalidation/replay against broader context reset after a known corrupted optional source while preserving frozen-request semantics.

long_horizon.o_fit: O explicitly rejects recall/explanation as capability evidence and is currently running a behavioral action-adherence comparison; the clean result directly validates that intermediate-proxy improvement can reverse across model generations.
long_horizon.scope: Reported long-horizon security intervention and tested Gemini generations; not a universal model-generation effect.
long_horizon.uncertainty: The causal bottleneck can change with model generation and environment.
long_horizon.decision_use: Require final task outcome after context/intervention changes and rerun causal assumptions when model identity changes.

long_horizon.o_fit: O has long-horizon plans and mutable decision state, but its evaluation coverage can benefit from explicit inheritance/update/counterfactual/rollback/composition patterns rather than static-context tasks.
long_horizon.scope: LongDS-Bench's 68 tasks and tested models; headline degradation does not identify one universal remedy.
long_horizon.uncertainty: Per-pattern intervention effects and deployable recovery mechanisms are not yet isolated.
long_horizon.decision_use: Use evolving-state task patterns as evaluation coverage and measure whether Context Kernel mechanisms reduce late-horizon state errors.

multi_agent.o_fit: O is not currently a multi-agent runtime, but task-conditioned pruning of roles/communication maps to future evaluator/search orchestration and avoids raw-N scaling.
multi_agent.scope: Mostly text benchmarks and gpt-4o-mini-style MAS; not long-horizon tool evidence.
multi_agent.uncertainty: Training the topology controller and transfer to O's tool/research workloads are unresolved.
multi_agent.decision_use: If O uses parallel roles, compare task-conditioned node/edge selection against fixed topology at matched cost before scaling team size.

multi_agent.o_fit: O already requires heterogeneous method search; the clean result gives direct evidence that the best outer search strategy changes by landscape and that QD can be best or worst under the same loop.
multi_agent.scope: Three autonomous ML-research domains with fixed untuned search strategies and finite execution budgets.
multi_agent.uncertainty: Landscape descriptors that predict the winning strategy are not yet validated as an online router.
multi_agent.decision_use: Treat Greedy/QD/Islands/etc. as conditional policies selected by landscape/evaluator properties, not as one default search architecture.

multi_agent.o_fit: Dynamic pruning supplies an accuracy-cost frontier if O later deploys multi-agent collaboration, but it does not address O's current evaluation/context bottleneck directly.
multi_agent.scope: ACL 2025 MAS benchmarks and learned node/edge dropout; high dropout eventually loses accuracy.
multi_agent.uncertainty: No evidence yet that the learned pruning policy transfers to O's long-horizon workflows.
multi_agent.decision_use: Retain as a future resource-allocation mechanism; never infer maximum pruning is optimal.

multi_agent.o_fit: O has protected held-out evaluation and needs hard-to-game evidence; evolving/diversifying adversaries or tests can reduce cyclic specialist overfit.
multi_agent.scope: Core War adversarial program evolution; MAP-Elites ablation is qualitative in the worker artifact and specialist statistics are domain-specific.
multi_agent.uncertainty: The marginal benefit of candidate diversity versus adversary-history diversity is not cleanly separated.
multi_agent.decision_use: For evaluator hardening, preserve diverse historical adversaries/tests and measure robustness against held-out opponent populations.

multi_agent.o_fit: Fixed-call heterogeneous mutation improves QD coverage in the worker source, but O does not yet need model-family parallelism to solve its current bottleneck.
multi_agent.scope: Core War QD search; model-family heterogeneity is confounded with other diversity axes and diminishing returns beyond four models are unresolved.
multi_agent.uncertainty: Cheaper prompt/role/sampling diversity may reproduce much of the benefit.
multi_agent.decision_use: Only consider model heterogeneity after a matched cheaper-diversity control shows correlated search channels remain a bottleneck.

multi_agent.o_fit: O's strategy favors heterogeneous search but does not yet measure effective-channel correlation; the clean evidence shows raw group size has sharply diminishing diversity and heterogeneity helps mainly when topology causes coupling.
multi_agent.scope: Open-ended idea generation and the tested model/topology conditions; prompt-tone ablation is not a full factorial across tool diversity.
multi_agent.uncertainty: Tool-heavy execution may have different coupling dynamics.
multi_agent.decision_use: Measure channel correlation/diversity first; prefer independent/blind initial exploration and add model heterogeneity only when a real diversity deficit is observed.

continual_learning.o_fit: O already makes context/candidate admission decisions; history-relative informativeness plus redundancy suppression is a transferable allocation principle even though literal Fisher-gradient selection targets continual tuning rather than O's current procedural state.
continual_learning.scope: Continual instruction tuning, mainly multimodal/text model experiments with last-layer gradient computation; not a universal forgetting optimizer.
continual_learning.uncertainty: Direct transfer to semantic artifact/context selection and its compute economics are untested; EMA beta and gradient cost matter.
continual_learning.decision_use: Test history-relative value and redundancy-aware selection for bounded candidate/context/evaluation budgets before considering any parameter-level implementation.

cross_field.o_fit: O already ranks actions by information value and repeatedly evaluates Candidates; adaptive replication allocation can directly reduce evaluation latency/cost versus equal repetition.
cross_field.scope: Classical OCBA evidence includes a 210-design stochastic simulation case; the large speedup is not universal and finite-budget pathologies exist.
cross_field.uncertainty: Safe finite-budget switching/racing rules for O-like evaluations need validation.
cross_field.decision_use: Allocate repeated evaluation budget toward close/noisy decision-critical candidates, with racing/elimination and an equal-allocation fallback at small or poorly estimated budgets.

cross_field.o_fit: O's selection metrics explicitly include decision-changing information value; dual-control evidence supplies a concrete mechanism for choosing actions that both perform and discriminate competing hypotheses.
cross_field.scope: Finite-hypothesis nonlinear control simulation with a reported model-selection delay reduction; not a generic research-loop effect size.
cross_field.uncertainty: Need an O-specific estimator of hypothesis discrimination value and a guard against costly probing after uncertainty is already low.
cross_field.decision_use: Prefer experiments whose outcomes separate live mechanism hypotheses, and decay probing once the decision posterior is sufficiently resolved.

cross_field.o_fit: O already switches routes on provider/coordination blocks; cause-aware restart/duplication is more directly useful to parallel evaluators/research workers than to O's single-writer control plane.
cross_field.scope: MapReduce-style production clusters and measurable task progress; whole-system gains combine multiple mechanisms.
cross_field.uncertainty: Agent/research stalls may not expose progress/cause signals comparable to cluster tasks.
cross_field.decision_use: Where parallel evaluation exists, diagnose stall cause and duplicate/restart only when expected latency saved exceeds resource and side-effect cost.

cross_field.o_fit: O retains traces and values diagnostic observability, but exhaustive logging/context can be expensive; sparse randomized instrumentation offers a tractable many-run diagnostic hypothesis.
cross_field.scope: Statistical software debugging over many executions; cited overhead savings are not an O diagnosis-time result.
cross_field.uncertainty: Requires enough repeated runs for aggregate signal and careful unbiased sampling.
cross_field.decision_use: Evaluate sparse diagnostic feature sampling for repeated campaigns while keeping authoritative control/effect records unsampled.

failure_evidence.o_fit: O may use verifiers to route search; the clean failure evidence shows verifier-selection error can compound with larger candidate budgets and underperform repeated sampling.
failure_evidence.scope: Specific math models, OVM/PRM verifiers, beam/search procedures and sample budgets; not all verifier-guided search.
failure_evidence.uncertainty: Crossover budget depends on verifier error and task distribution.
failure_evidence.decision_use: Benchmark verifier-guided search against equal-compute repeated sampling and monitor valid-branch pruning as budget scales.

failure_evidence.o_fit: O already protects evidence integrity; verifier-compatible shortcut learning is a direct threat whenever an acceptance signal under-specifies the intended invariant.
failure_evidence.scope: Inductive-rule RLVR with extensional verification; shortcut rates do not generalize to fully specified rewards.
failure_evidence.uncertainty: Which invariance transformations best expose O-specific reward shortcuts must be designed per task family.
failure_evidence.decision_use: Use isomorphic/adversarial transformations and second-signal checks before treating a verifiable reward as capability evidence.

failure_evidence.o_fit: The current O unit explicitly distinguishes action adherence from static/verbal quality; clean evidence shows better offline verifier precision/recall can fail to improve or can regress the optimized policy.
failure_evidence.scope: Qwen2.5-7B mathematical RL and the tested verifiers; not a universal model-verifier ordering.
failure_evidence.uncertainty: Optimization-induced distribution shift varies by verifier and policy family.
failure_evidence.decision_use: Select evaluators by downstream optimized-policy outcomes under matched conditions, not fixed-set classifier metrics alone.

failure_evidence.o_fit: O uses coding/repository tasks and held-out machinery; weak tests and answer leakage can turn benchmark PASS into false capability evidence.
failure_evidence.scope: Audited SWE-Agent+GPT-4 successful patches and specific SWE-bench versions; not a universal coding-agent failure rate.
failure_evidence.uncertainty: Some contamination risk is inferred from issue age rather than proven training exposure.
failure_evidence.decision_use: Audit task leakage and semantic oracle strength, and preserve hidden/stronger tests before counting coding benchmarks as capability evidence.

failure_evidence.o_fit: O needs independent, materially different evidence; a static benchmark potentially reflecting model memory makes temporal/decontaminated alternatives decision-relevant.
failure_evidence.scope: Localization probes across SWE-bench Verified, BeetleBox, and SWE-rebench on two Claude models; evidence is circumstantial, not proof of memorization.
failure_evidence.uncertainty: Benchmark difficulty and training exposure are confounded.
failure_evidence.decision_use: Use newer/temporal benchmark controls and compare rank/order shifts before attributing static SWE-bench gains to agent architecture.

failure_evidence.o_fit: O's evidence gate depends on mechanically judged outcomes; observed benchmark-verifier hackability makes adversarial verifier auditing a direct prerequisite to trusting external evaluation.
failure_evidence.scope: Five audited terminal-agent suites and tested hacker-fixer access conditions; residual attack rate remains suite-dependent.
failure_evidence.uncertainty: Hardening may overfit known exploit families and adaptive attacks can remain.
failure_evidence.decision_use: Adversarially attack evaluators before adoption, retain held-out exploit sets, and report residual exploitability rather than binary hardened/not-hardened status.

failure_evidence.o_fit: O's Candidate evidence is scope-bound; cross-task verifier failure directly supports per-target admission rather than treating verifier strength as a global scalar.
failure_evidence.scope: Recent single-author VLM/self-DPO preprint across MathVista/MMMU/BLINK and two students; high-value warning, not universal law.
failure_evidence.uncertainty: Independent replication and text-only/RLVR transfer are unresolved.
failure_evidence.decision_use: Measure verifier quality on the exact target distribution and retain baseline fallback when target-task calibration is poor.

failure_evidence.o_fit: O already tests recovery from injected transient tool failure; WAREX supplies stronger realistic network/server fault evidence and shows generic recovery prompting is not uniformly effective.
failure_evidence.scope: WebArena, REAL, WebVoyager with controlled network/server faults and tested scaffolds; relative drops are benchmark-specific.
failure_evidence.uncertainty: Fault distributions and production retry/idempotency behavior differ from web benchmarks.
failure_evidence.decision_use: Extend long-horizon evaluation with matched realistic transport/server faults and measure final outcome recovery, not merely retry behavior.

failure_evidence.o_fit: O requires defensible independent evidence; an official benchmark scaffold leaking test examples shows that benchmark code provenance alone is insufficient.
failure_evidence.scope: The affected TAU-bench Few Shot scaffold/file; does not invalidate all TAU-bench results.
failure_evidence.uncertainty: Leakage prevalence across other official scaffolds is unknown.
failure_evidence.decision_use: Before expensive external runs, inspect default demonstrations/retrieval caches/test fixtures and execution logs for contamination.

failure_evidence.o_fit: O learns Candidates from failures; environment/scaffold/interface barriers can otherwise be misattributed to policy and produce harmful learning.
failure_evidence.scope: Observational HAL analysis of failed AssistantBench/CORE-Bench/SciCode tasks; presence of a barrier is not proof it caused the failure.
failure_evidence.uncertainty: Causal attribution requires replay or controlled environment repair.
failure_evidence.decision_use: Classify policy versus environment/oracle/interface failure before generating improvement Candidates; use controlled reruns when attribution is ambiguous.

failure_evidence.o_fit: O optimizes elapsed time and evidence value; non-monotonic reasoning effort supports treating test-time compute as a conditional knob rather than an assumed improvement.
failure_evidence.scope: 36 HAL model-agent-benchmark cells; 21 were equal/lower under more reasoning, while 15 improved.
failure_evidence.uncertainty: Cost, scaffold interaction, and task mix explain part of heterogeneity.
failure_evidence.decision_use: Estimate per-task/scaffold reasoning-effort curves under matched outcomes/cost before increasing inference budget.

scientist_agents.o_fit: O's objective explicitly minimizes elapsed time and values decision-changing evidence; the clean worker shows cross-system research quality is not monotonic in raw token/cost while within-workflow scaling can still help.
scientist_agents.scope: MLReplicate/ASI-Bench cross-system comparisons are confounded by architecture/model differences; not evidence against matched test-time scaling.
scientist_agents.uncertainty: Workflow-specific scaling curves and architecture-versus-compute causal decomposition remain incomplete.
scientist_agents.decision_use: Compare architecture/mechanism changes at matched compute, then separately measure within-workflow scaling curves before buying more budget as a substitute for better workflow design.

neuroscience.o_fit: The local-learning mechanism targets parameter-training substrate, while O's immediate bottlenecks are external evidence, context/action behavior, and evaluator integrity; O has no matching weight-training path to test it now.
neuroscience.scope: ICML 2025 MLP/CNN/RNN biological-plausibility benchmarks; not continual-learning or autonomous-agent evidence.
neuroscience.uncertainty: No independent replication located and sequential character prediction remains well below backpropagation.
neuroscience.decision_use: Retain as distant training-substrate research; do not consume current O implementation/evaluation budget.

reasoning.o_fit: O already has failure traces, restart-safe execution, and strategy review; value-guided allocation between fresh attempts and diagnostic repair is directly transferable to bounded coding/formal tasks.
reasoning.scope: Lean theorem proving with compiler feedback and fixed sampling budgets; not general agent repair evidence.
reasoning.uncertainty: The learned value/router and repair model are domain-specific, and token accounting differs between restart and refinement.
reasoning.decision_use: Test a matched-budget router choosing fresh attempt versus bounded diagnostic repair after failures, rather than unconditional restart or unconditional repair.

reasoning.o_fit: O's heterogeneous search policy can use structural branch diversity before local repair, but the clean study lacks a same-compute i.i.d. control and is outside Lean/O workflows.
reasoning.scope: Why3 program verification with four task-equivalent structural variants and bounded repair; semantic equivalence across variants is not formally proven.
reasoning.uncertainty: Marginal value of structural diversity versus simply four stochastic samples remains unresolved.
reasoning.decision_use: Only elevate after a matched i.i.d.-sampling control; retain as a composite experiment design.

reasoning.o_fit: Specialized repair training can beat scale on a narrow task, but O currently does not train a dedicated repair LM and needs end-to-end evidence rather than isolated synthetic repair accuracy.
reasoning.scope: Synthetic Lean proof mutations and single-shot repair; no demonstrated pass@K system gain.
reasoning.uncertainty: Natural failure transfer and end-to-end effect are unknown.
reasoning.decision_use: Retain for a future repair-model substrate only after end-to-end integration evidence or a concrete O training route exists.

reasoning.o_fit: O's Context Kernel explicitly routes optional context; repository-scale proof evidence shows full-repository context can be worse than selected dependencies, directly supporting selection over dumping.
reasoning.scope: Lean repository verification; curated dependency context is an oracle derived from ground-truth proof dependencies, not a deployable selector.
reasoning.uncertainty: A learned/heuristic selector must approximate oracle dependencies without target leakage while retaining useful analogies.
reasoning.decision_use: Benchmark deployable optional-context selection against full-context and oracle-dependency upper bound on repository tasks, with explicit leakage controls and behavioral outcomes.

immediate_decision_relevance_order.reason: These directly address O's current revision-22 action-adherence uncertainty and guard against declaring context/control improvements from static metrics.
Independent evidence is O's major bottleneck; contamination, weak oracles, environment faults, and attribution errors can make that evidence misleading.
O has implemented Context Kernel provenance/routing machinery but still needs behavioral evidence that selected context supports correct evolving state and action.
These can reduce elapsed time by spending scarce evaluations on discriminating hypotheses and using strategy/budget conditional on landscape uncertainty.
O already has durable restart semantics; the remaining decision value is whether coherent scoped restoration and selective repair improve recovery without replaying irreversible effects.

non_immediate: Weight-training/neuroscience mechanisms remain low priority until O has a concrete trainable substrate and matched evaluation route.
Raw multi-agent/model-count scaling is not a current priority; evidence favors conditional topology/diversity allocation and strong single-agent/multi-output controls.
No relevance judgment here is fed back into clean exploration workers.
